newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares end active trading day weaker.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares end active trading day weaker.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares ended an active trading day weaker on Monday as most foreign investors continued profit-taking in selected stock.

Brokers said an on-going strike by junior doctors and nurses pressing for higher salaries and better working conditions coupled with the threat of a nationwide demonstration organised by the Zimbabwe Congress of Trade Unions (ZCTU) to pressure the government into resolving the health crisis had not yet visibly impacted on the market.
"The strike hasn't really affected the market yet but I don't think it's helping investor sentiment at all," commented one.
Monday's losers included tea and coffee growers EHPL, sugar producer Hippo and tobbaco firm TSL, all 10 cents down at 140, 890 and 590 respectively while pork processor Colcom shed 15 cents to 370.

Others to fall were plate and glass company PGI, 20 cents down at 510, timber producer Border which lost 25 to 1,300, horticultural group Ariston which eased 40 cents to 1,500, newspaper group Zimpapers and financiers Finhold, both 50 cents lower at 2,000 and 900 respectively and bankers FMB, 200 cents down at 4,200.

Against the trend, tyre firm NTS, and household furniture and clothing retailer Tedco both added 5 cents to 470 and 615 respectively, cement company Porthold went up 25 cents to 1,325 and clothing retailer Edgars added 50 cents to 3,250.
The 57-counter industril index lost 31.60 points to 7,945.64.

Minings were quiet with gold producer Rio Tinto 100 cents up at 3,600 while another gold firm, Falcon and copper miners Mhangura lost 25 and 50 cents to 15 and 1,650 respectively. The seven-share index eased by 1.88 points to 1229.01
